synth.overview:
Ranked against the decks that matter now. These are the four being built: The Free Peoples (casual/the-free-peoples, rev 15), Izzet Otters (casual/izzet-prowess, rev 6), Finneas (commander/finneas-rabbits) and Gandalf and the Valley (commander/gandalf-and-the-valley). User2's, User3's and User4's three built Commander decks count too. Rabbits, Gruul, Giada, Gisa and the other casual lists are all status 'idea' (checked with `python -m decklab.db deck list`).

Three findings shape the order:
1. **No baseline for the current lists.** Every one of the 80 saved results predates the 2026-10-05 rework and is marked earlier engine, and `forge cards` says "No card data yet" for TFP, Izzet, Finneas and Gandalf. So no misplay can be confirmed on today's lists before a fresh card-logged baseline.
2. **The worst misplays are in User1's 60-card deck, TFP.** Fires of Mount Doom is cast 0.0% of 837 drawn copies. You Cannot Pass! is cast 8.0% of 880. Éowyn x2 is cast 46% in the experiment control and 88% with an override. Samwise is cast 19%, Gandalf the White 45% and Gimli's Fury 46%. The 'etb' override set already measured +5.8 pts [+3.3, +8.3] for TFP against Izzet and missed adoption only on early-in-hand low ends for Massacre Wurm and Palace Jailer. Massacre Wurm is in no current deck.
3. **Every fork AI change today means a new engine and a full replay**, and the fork has no switch to A/B one change. A small fork-side switch hook, wired to Deck Lab's existing Pilots `-dlpilot` per-seat switches, lets each Java fix ship default-off. It can then be measured paired in one build and adopted per list, which makes it the enabler for the Java fixes.

Two items were confirmed in source during this pass:
- ComputerUtilCard.java:1261-1263 ("interrupt 2: remove blocker to save my attacker") requires `!ph.isPlayerTurn(ai)` and also that the removal target `c` is among the blockers. On the opponent's turn the blockers are the AI's own creatures, so in 1v1 this branch can never fire for removal aimed at an opposing creature. It looks inverted, and it hurts every combat-timed removal spell, You Cannot Pass! included.
- primal_might.txt has `PlayMain1:TRUE` but no `AILogic$ Fight`, while PumpAi.java:129/361/460-461 routes to FightAi.canFight only for AILogic Fight or PowerDmg.

The upstream cherry-picks barely touch current decks: only Darkwater Catacombs and Dimir Signet are affected, both in the idea deck Alela. Counterspell mana-holding matters little now that Izzet's counters are in the sideboard. Team-pump work mainly helps Rabbits, an idea deck. So all three rank low despite earlier effort on them.

candidates.title: Card-logged baseline of the current lists (prerequisite)
candidates.evidence: All 80 results in decklab/data/forge/results are dated 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-04 and marked earlier engine. `python -m decklab.lib.forge cards` reports 'No card data yet' for Izzet Otters, TFP, Gandalf and the Valley, Finneas and Gruul. The cast rates used to rank misplays come from older lists (TFP sha d07f234f, vs Angels only).
candidates.change: No code. Run `python -m decklab.lib.forge field casual/the-free-peoples`, `field casual/izzet-prowess`, `field commander/finneas-rabbits` and `field commander/gandalf-and-the-valley` (or `replay`) with the card log on. Run them serially on an idle PC.
candidates.measure: About 1,600-3,000 games per deck. Constructed pairs run at about 1,000-1,400 games a minute and Commander at about 230, so roughly 30-60 idle minutes in all. Output: per-card cast share against the deck median, which confirms or re-ranks C2-C9.
candidates.expected_value: High. It gives trustworthy current win rates and per-card evidence for every later A/B, and it is the control the experiments pair against.
candidates.decks_helped: TFP, Izzet Otters, Finneas, Gandalf and the Valley
candidates.risks: Results get re-keyed again if a fork engine change follows. That's acceptable, since the baseline doubles as each experiment's control.

candidates.title: Adopt a TFP-scoped ETB override set (Fires, Éowyn, Samwise, Palace Jailer)
candidates.evidence: The etb set (overrides/sets.json:22-93) measured +3.0 pts [+1.6, +4.3] pooled and +5.8 [+3.3, +8.3] for Free Peoples vs Izzet. Cast rates: Fires 0% to 54.3%, Éowyn 46.3% to 88.4% (+10.2 pts win when in hand early [+4.4, +16.0]), Jailer 84.7% to 90.1%. It was blocked only by early-in-hand low ends of -5.5 (Massacre Wurm) and -4.9 (Palace Jailer) against the -3 rule (sim-wave3-contract.md:1620). Massacre Wurm and Théoden aren't in any current deck. Samwise's OptionalDecider edit was never measured on its own. Samwise is cast 19.4% of 1,106 in Fellowship data.
candidates.change: Add a new set 'etb-tfp' in decklab/lib/forge/overrides/sets.json. It holds only Fires of Mount Doom (AILogic Always on the ChompEquip sub; the etb-flagged variant reached 75.8% cast but its low end was -10.1, so keep the narrower edit), Éowyn, Fearless Knight (BadETB), Samwise (OptionalDecider You) and, as a separate arm, Palace Jailer (BadETB).
candidates.measure: Experiment with arms etb-tfp and etb-tfp+jailer. Pairs: TFP vs Izzet Otters (current lists), plus TFP vs one other reference. Run 1,600 paired games a pair, rising to the 2,800 the analysis asked for if it's still 'more games'. Fast Constructed pairs mean about 10-20 idle minutes.
candidates.effort: Low (JSON plus card-script copies that already exist)
candidates.expected_value: Highest per hour: about +3 to +6 pts on User1's main deck, through a fix already measured once.
candidates.decks_helped: The Free Peoples (also Giada's Sunblast Angel later, through etb-flagged)
candidates.risks: Fires gets cast into an empty board for its damage only, and Jailer may be cast early for a worse target. The per-card early-in-hand measure guards against both. Superseded by C4 if that lands.

candidates.title: Fork switch hook so Java AI fixes ship default-off and A/B in one build
candidates.evidence: Every fork commit is a new engine (HISTORY.md:663; engine.py ENGINE_FIELDS), so every result is re-keyed and needs a replay (the last full replay was 26,094 games). `-Ddecklab.gamePatches=off` is all-or-nothing and also turns off deck-order-1, which paired tests need (Match.java:37, variants.py:65,71). Pilots.java switches work per seat but live in Deck Lab's jar, which forge-ai classes can't call. The Gisa/Bontu fix (af513b9fd) was judged on 100 unpaired games, is ungated, and isn't listed in forge-patches.txt.
candidates.change: Fork: add forge-ai/src/main/java/forge/ai/AiSwitches.java, a static `on(Player, String id)` defaulting to false, in the style of AiSignals and LibraryOrder. Have decklab Startup.java register Pilots.on into it, and let simjar.PILOT_SWITCHES, pilots.SWITCH_WORDS and Pilots.AVAILABLE accept fork ids. Each later Java fix in C4-C7 checks `AiSwitches.on(ai, "<id>")`. Also gate af513b9fd behind an id. Optionally test a config arm whose `forge_dir` points at a second install (install.py --out) for unswitchable changes.
candidates.measure: No sims needed beyond cardlog-check (12 Constructed + 3 Commander games x4) and test_forge_aipatches.py. One-time cost: one replay of all matchups for the new engine (about 26k games, 1-2 idle hours). After that, fork AI fixes cost a paired experiment, not a replay.
candidates.effort: Medium (about a day: fork class, Startup wiring, three switch lists and a test)
candidates.expected_value: Enabler. It cuts each Java fix's cost from build + replay to build + one paired arm, and makes default-off fixes adoptable per list.
candidates.risks: Every fork build still has to pass cardlog-check and update the CHECKED constants (simjar.py:84-91). Keep the switch check cheap in hot paths.

candidates.title: Fix optional or empty-target ETB and sub-ability vetoes in Java (ChangeZoneAi, DestroyAllAi, checkETBEffects)
candidates.evidence: ChangeZoneAi.java:1141-1147 allows doWithoutTarget only for planeswalker +counter abilities, so a `TargetMin$ 0` sub with no candidates vetoes the parent. That is Fiery Annihilation's bug (its override moved the cast rate 0% to 90%, and removing it cost -3.2 pts [-4.7, -1.6]) and Samwise's. DestroyAllAi.java:76-77 returns CantPlayAi on an empty opponent list, which is why Fires of Mount Doom is cast 0.0% of 837 and Sunblast Angel 26.5%. AiController.java:357-361's escape needs not-fully-targetable plus (in danger or BadETB), and isFullyTargetable is true for TargetMin 0.
candidates.change:
Fork, behind switch id etb-harmless-1:
- ChangeZoneAi.java:1141: treat a `getMinTargets()==0` AbilitySub with no candidates as doWithoutTarget.
- DestroyAllAi.java:76: when `sa.isTrigger()` or it is a sub, and both lists are empty, return WillPlay.
- AiController.java:359-361: skip the veto when the trigger's minimum targets is 0 or it has no candidates.
Keep the Éowyn/Jailer-style 'must target an opponent's creature' cases out by default, or opt them in with BadETB, to avoid the Ravenous Chupacabra 'cast as a bare body' question.
candidates.measure: After C3: a pilot arm for TFP (and Gisa/Giada as references) on C1's control seeds, 1,600 paired games a pair, card-logged for the Fires and Samwise cast share, plus a mirror. About 30-40 idle minutes.
candidates.effort: Medium (3 small hunks, a scenario test, the switch)
candidates.expected_value: High. It replaces C2's Fires and Samwise overrides and the adopted fiery override with a class fix, and covers future cards (Plague Belcher, Victimize-style riders).
candidates.decks_helped: TFP; Giada and Gisa later; any deck with optional rider subs
candidates.risks: A broad veto change may make other ETB creatures cast into worthless states. Watch reference pairs and the early-in-hand low ends.

candidates.title: Fix the inverted 'interrupt 2' in useRemovalNow (combat removal after blocks)
candidates.evidence: ComputerUtilCard.java:1261-1263 (read in this pass): `if (ph.is(COMBAT_DECLARE_BLOCKERS) && !ph.isPlayerTurn(ai)) { ... currCombat.getAllBlockers().contains(c)`, where c is the opposing creature being removed. On the opponent's turn the blockers are the AI's, so it can never match in 1v1. It should be `ph.isPlayerTurn(ai)`: the opponent's blocker is stopping the AI's attacker. You Cannot Pass!, which can only target a creature in a blocking pair, is cast 8.0% of 880 drawn and stuck 91.8%. After declare blockers the threat value is also multiplied by 0.1 (:1365-1371).
candidates.change: Fork, behind switch id removal-in-combat-1: flip the condition at ComputerUtilCard.java:1262 to `ph.isPlayerTurn(ai)`. Optionally add the mirror case (on the opponent's turn, remove an attacker blocked by the AI's legendary when that saves the blocker). Add a scenario test in forge-gui-desktop/src/test/java/forge/ai, modelled on DestroyAiTest.
candidates.measure: Pilot arm for TFP vs Izzet and TFP vs one other list, 1,600 paired games, card-logged You Cannot Pass! / Swords to Plowshares / Path to Exile cast share and turn. About 15-20 idle minutes after C3.
candidates.effort: Low to medium (a one-line fix plus a test; check upstream git blame first)
candidates.expected_value: Medium-high. It is a real upstream bug affecting all single-target removal in combat. You Cannot Pass! alone is about 2.3 on the evidence report's misplay score.
candidates.decks_helped: TFP mainly; every deck with instant removal
candidates.risks: Removal may be spent mid-combat on small blockers instead of saved for threats. Watch Swords and Path cast timing. Also worth offering upstream.

candidates.title: Prowess and spells-matter sequencing: cast cheap noncreature spells before attacks
candidates.evidence: Izzet Otters' current main deck: Stormcatch Mentor x2, Coruscation Mage x2, Firespitter Whelp x2, Thieving Otter x3, Bria, Guttersnipe, plus 4 Preordain, 3 Burst Lightning, 3 Flame Lash, 2 Pearl of Wisdom. Upstream issue #6617 (open since 2024): the AI casts noncreature spells after combat even with prowess out. DrawAi.java:169-173 won't draw before Main 2 (Preordain, Pearl, Mind Spring 43.1%). The hints override's BuffedBy on Stormcatch Mentor and Heartfire Immolator changed nothing (+0.2, +0.0), so data hints don't reach this.
candidates.change: Fork, behind switch id prowess-precombat-1. In AiController.getSpellAbilityToPlay, during MAIN1, when the AI controls an untapped creature that will attack and has prowess or a 'whenever you cast a noncreature spell' trigger, let cheap cantrips and burn through: relax DrawAi's MAIN2 gate at :169-173 and prefer them before creature spells. Use the existing PlayMain1 path where possible.
candidates.measure: First check C1's data for Izzet's Preordain and Pearl cast phase and turn (the card log has turn, not phase; may need C9). Then a pilot arm Izzet vs TFP plus a mirror, 1,600-3,200 games, about 20-30 idle minutes.
candidates.effort: Medium-high (new heuristic; needs a scenario test)
candidates.expected_value: Medium-high for Matt's main 60-card deck. It is the one current deck whose plan Forge mis-sequences by design.
candidates.risks: Spending removal precombat when it should be held. Limit it to cantrips and to burn aimed at the face or a blocker.

candidates.title: Flash creatures: reserve mana or cast in Main 2 instead of end-step only
candidates.evidence: PermanentCreatureAi.java:174-176 returns `canCastAtOppTurn ? isEOTBeforeMyTurn : isOwnEOT`, under 'TODO: maybe implement a way to reserve mana' at :175. Gandalf the White is cast 44.9% of 845 drawn. The PlayMain1 override raised that to 90.2%, but the matchup moved -0.5 [-2.2, +1.1] and Gandalf's win when drawn -2.7 [-12.4, +6.9]: casting it main-phase is not clearly better. Gandalf, Friend of the Shire (Gandalf and the Valley) and Cathar Commando (Finneas) share the path. Samwise also has flash.
candidates.change: Fork, behind switch id flash-reserve-1: in doAdvancedFlashLogic, when it is the AI's Main 2, canPayCost holds and nothing better was cast, call reserveManaSources with a new per-turn memory set that clears at the AI's own end step (PhaseHandler.java:363). Then hold the lands and cast at the opponent's end step. Fallback: a new AiProps FLASH_CHANCE_TO_CAST_NO_ETB_IN_MAIN2. The same set later serves counterspells (C10).
candidates.measure: Pilot arm for TFP and Gandalf and the Valley, 1,600 paired games each, card-logged cast share and turn. Gandalf and the Valley is Commander (about 230 games a minute), so about 20-30 idle minutes.
candidates.expected_value: Medium-low. Evidence that the fix wins games is weak, but it is shared infrastructure with C10.
candidates.decks_helped: TFP, Gandalf and the Valley, Finneas
candidates.risks: Holding mana delays developing the board. The override data already hints the gain is small.

candidates.title: One-line script hints for current Commander decks: Primal Might Fight logic, Puca's Mischief
candidates.evidence: primal_might.txt (read in this pass) has no AILogic, so PumpAi treats it as a plain pump. Fight handling is only for AILogic Fight or PowerDmg (PumpAi.java:129, :361, :460-461). It was cast 37.6% of 359 against Finneas's 82.5% median; Rabid Bite (PowerDmg) was cast 73.8% of 4,598. Puca's Mischief has AI:RemoveDeck:All (p/pucas_mischief.txt:7), so it is never cast (AiController.java:1568).
candidates.change: Add an override set 'cmdr-hints' in decklab/lib/forge/overrides/sets.json: `AILogic$ Fight` on Primal Might's SP$ Pump line (check that FightAi.canFight handles the X pump), and remove `AI:RemoveDeck:All` from Puca's Mischief after reading ControlExchangeAi.java for its upkeep exchange.
candidates.measure: Experiment pair Finneas vs Gandalf and the Valley (both current Commander decks), 1,600 paired games, with cast targets for both cards. About 15 idle minutes at about 230 games a minute.
candidates.expected_value: Low-medium: 1 card in each of two 100-card decks, but nearly free.
candidates.risks: Fight with X=0 may fight badly. Puca's Mischief may swap away a good permanent. Watch the early-in-hand low end.

candidates.title: Opt-in AI decision log for named cards
candidates.evidence: The card log records card moves only (DeckLabSim.java). Nothing records castable-but-declined with its AiPlayDecision. AiSignals counts only timeouts. Diagnosing Overrun holding, the ETB veto, flash and prowess timing currently takes thousands of games. Upstream open PR #12180 adds an opt-in AI decision log.
candidates.change: Fork: a `-Ddecklab.decisionLog=<card names>` hook in AiController.canPlayAndPayFor and saSideEffects (and the attack-declaration result) that writes one line per decision: card, phase, decision and reason. Deck Lab's experiment.py can then count cast opportunities as a denominator. Consider adapting PR #12180.
candidates.measure: No sims beyond a few dozen seeded games to validate. Then use it for C5 and C6 diagnosis in a few hundred games instead of thousands.
candidates.expected_value: Medium. It speeds diagnosis for C5-C7 and C11 and says why a card was held, not just how often.
candidates.risks: Log volume and speed. Keep it off by default and filtered by name.

candidates.title: Finish team-pump-1 (mirror and card log) and move TeamPumpAi into the fork
candidates.evidence: Rabbits vs Vampires +4.1 pts [+2.5, +5.7], 1.02x speed, timeouts 0/800 vs 4/800 (REPORT.md:678-682). Not adopted: no mirror, and the arm wasn't card-logged. Current decks with team pumps: only Boromir, Warden of the Tower (TFP ability). Make a Stand (Giada) and Rabbits are idea decks. It still lives in Deck Lab's jar by reflection (AiPatches.java:55-65), and open upstream PR #11124 also edits PumpAllAi.
candidates.change: Run the mirror plus a card-logged Rabbits pair. Then port teamPumpWorthIt (TeamPumpAi.java:76-161) into PumpAllAi.java before :131 behind the C3 switch, and add TRICK_ATTACKERS marking for instant pumps (ComputerUtilCard.java:1840-1851 pattern).
candidates.measure: Mirror at 3,200 games (unpaired, about ±2.4 pts) plus a card-logged Rabbits vs Vampires 1,600: about 40-60 idle minutes at 157 games a minute.
candidates.effort: Low to adopt as is; medium to port
candidates.expected_value: Low for current decks; moderate if Rabbits or Giada come back.
candidates.risks: The mirror may stay at 'more games'. The port would conflict with upstream PR #11124 if that merges before the 2.0.16 rebase.

candidates.title: Go-wide attack surplus rule
candidates.evidence: AiAttackController.java:1142-1145 decrements the AI's ratio once per opposing blocker. shouldAttack/SpellAbilityFactors (:1376-1565) judges each attacker against every blocker alone. Worked example: six 1/1s vs two 2/2s gives aggression 2, and nothing attacks. Profile proxies: Rabbits on Reckless +2.8 [+0.9, +4.8], Gruul on Reckless +2.9. Milestone 0 measured Rabbits attacking on 38.8% of turns, 49.4% on Reckless.
candidates.change: Fork, behind switch id go-wide-1: after the aggression is set at :1273, compute the surplus attackers beyond what the opponent can block (notNeededAsBlockers pool minus the maximum number of blocks). If the guaranteed damage is at least 4 or at least a third of the opponent's life, raise aggression to 4 or 5.
candidates.measure: It touches every game, so pairing couples less. Mirrors for Finneas, TFP and Izzet at about 3,200 games, plus reference pairs: about 1-2 idle hours.
candidates.effort: Medium-high (core combat; needs scenario tests in BasicAttackTests style)
candidates.expected_value: Medium and broad: token decks (Finneas, Gandalf's Junimos) under-attack today. Uncertain until measured.
candidates.decks_helped: Finneas, Gandalf and the Valley, TFP; Rabbits later
candidates.risks: Overextending into crack-backs. Could shift ratings toward aggro, so check ranking stability (Spearman) as G3 did.

candidates.title: Cherry-pick upstream AI fixes now (mana and lethal-trigger commits)
candidates.evidence: `git apply --check` is clean against decklab for 5198ca74c, 8c4a3ee45 (+ e9fa54ac2 after it), ef12bf2e4 and 0bd294690. Only Darkwater Catacombs and Dimir Signet (Alela, an idea deck) are user-deck cards among the scripts changed upstream. None fixes a known weakness. The 2.0.16 rebase is planned for about mid-November (PLAN.md:45).
candidates.change: Defer to the 2.0.16 rebase. Pick early only if Alela becomes a building deck.
candidates.measure: It changes the engine, so a full replay (about 26k games) with no paired A/B. Not worth an idle slot now.
candidates.risks: Compile compatibility with 2.0.15's forge-game is unchecked. 2342d00b5 and a69da2b83 touch broad forge-game files.

recommended_first_steps: 1. Queue C1, a card-logged baseline of the four current lists (TFP, Izzet Otters, Finneas, Gandalf and the Valley), behind the idle gate. Run it serially, roughly 30-60 minutes. It refreshes the stale results and becomes the control for every later arm.

2. Same queue: the C2 experiment (etb-tfp, with and without Palace Jailer, TFP vs Izzet at 1,600 paired games, about 15 minutes) and the C8 cmdr-hints set (Finneas vs Gandalf at 1,600 games, about 15 minutes). Both are data-only and adoptable within the session.

3. While those run, build C3 (the AiSwitches hook plus a gate on Gisa/Bontu) in the fork, with a scenario-test scaffold from upstream AITest/DestroyAiTest. Run cardlog-check, then accept one replay for the new engine.

4. Then implement C5 (flip ComputerUtilCard.java:1262, the smallest and most certain bug) and C4 (optional or empty-target vetoes) as default-off switches, each with a scenario test. A/B them as pilot arms on TFP. If C4 wins, retire the Fires and Samwise overrides.
5. Next is C6 (prowess sequencing for Izzet Otters), with C9's decision log if C1's data can't show cast phase. C7, C10, C11 and C12 come after, as idle time allows.
questions_for_owner: Should fork AI fixes ship default-off behind per-list pilot switches (adopted per deck through simulation.json), or default-on so the install itself is the adoption? C3 assumes default-off.
Can C2 adopt only the Éowyn, Samwise and Fires edits if Palace Jailer's early-in-hand low end stays below -3, or must the set pass as a whole?

Is a one-time replay of all matchups (about 26k games, 1-2 idle hours) acceptable for the C3 engine change, given the baseline in C1 would otherwise be re-keyed shortly after? Option: do C3 first, then C1 on the new engine.
Should the ComputerUtilCard.java:1262 fix (C5) also be offered upstream as a PR?
Is Izzet Otters' plan meant to be prowess-first (cantrips before attacks)? That decides whether C6 is worth its medium-high effort.
Is matt439/forge's decklab branch pushed? `git branch -vv` shows no upstream for it.

verified.confidence: High on the evidence and plan corrections. I checked them with read-only commands: forge status, cards, field --dry-run, replay --dry-run and a JSON scan of the results. I did not check the TFP sha d07f234f claim.
verified.corrections:
The core claim holds: there is no card-logged baseline for the current lists, and C1 is the right prerequisite. The plan is still wrong in several places.

Evidence I could confirm:
- decklab/data/forge/results holds 80 top-level result JSONs. By their `created` field: 12 from 2026-10-01, 25 from 2026-10-02, 13 from 2026-10-03 and 29 from 2026-10-04 (79 parsed with that field). results/field/ holds 2 more field notes.
- `python -m decklab.lib.forge cards` prints "No card data yet." for casual/the-free-peoples, casual/izzet-prowess, commander/finneas-rabbits, commander/gandalf-and-the-valley and casual/gruul-ramp.
- `replay --dry-run` lists 20 matchups (23,280 games). Every one says "with today's 0", so the saved results really are all from the earlier engine.
- `forge status` shows engine 2.0.15-decklab-d84031a6d, with the card log on and ready.

Corrections:
1. "(or `replay`)" is wrong. Replay only re-plays saved matchups whose lists are still current (decklab/lib/forge/cli_results.py:64-98). None of its 20 matchups involves TFP, Izzet Otters, Finneas or Gandalf; they are Angels, Zombies, Vampires, Rabbits, Lightning Aggro, Gisa v Giada and so on. Replay cannot produce this baseline, so `field` is the only route. Running replay would cost about 28 minutes on decks that aren't the targets.
2. "With the card log on" needs no flag. The card log is already on by default ("card log: on (per-card stats)" in status). `field` has no card-log option, and its results are saved as ordinary matchup results, which `cards` reads.
3. The game counts are wrong. At the default standard budget, `field --dry-run` gives:
   - TFP: 10 opponents x about 400 = about 4,000 games, 25-31 min.
   - Izzet: about 4,000 games, 25-31 min.
   - Finneas: 5 opponents, about 2,000 games, 9-10 min.
   - Gandalf: about 2,000 games, 9-10 min.
   TFP and Izzet each include the other, and so do Finneas and Gandalf, so about 11,200 unique games. That is roughly 65-80 minutes in all, not 30-60, and 4,000 per constructed deck is outside the 1,600-3,000 the plan states.
4. The constructed speed is wrong. "1,000-1,400 games a minute" is the fastest pair only: Izzet v Gruul, warm, 1,426.3 g/min (decklab/forge-trial/sim-investigation.md:20). The same line gives Rabbits v Vampires (constructed) at 157.3 g/min. The estimator's own figure for TFP's field works out to about 130-160 g/min (4,000 games in 25-31 min). Commander at about 230 matches (232.6 on line 20).
5. Fields are mostly idea decks. TFP's 10 opponents are mostly idea-status lists; only Izzet Otters is in progress ('building'), and Lightning Aggro is a product. The Commander fields are Alela, Gisa, Giada and Yoshimaru (all idea) plus the other building deck. The baseline therefore measures the decks against unbuilt lists, and the plan should say so. If C2-C9 hinge on particular cards, use `--opponents` to target the pairs that matter.
6. Gruul is named in the evidence but isn't in the run list. It only appears as a TFP/Izzet opponent, so its own card data won't come from this run unless `field casual/gruul-ramp` is added.
7. Following the forge-sims-serial rule, run them one after another in the main session with the running server's warm pool (not `--local` in parallel). Use `field --dry-run` first to confirm the plan.

verified.confidence: medium-high. All the cited numbers check out against the 2026-10-03 reports, and the decision point in Forge's source is the right one. Several supporting claims are wrong or out of date, and the expected value comes from old decklists.

FATAL FLAW: a default-off switch does not stop a new commit from re-keying every result.
- ENGINE_FIELDS includes "forge" (decklab/lib/forge/engine.py:133-134). _engine() sets it from the version (engine.py:321).

- HISTORY.md:663 says the same: "each commit is an engine and a card-log check of its own".
- So each later C4-C7 Java fix is a new fork commit and a new build name. Even with the fix default-off, every saved result becomes "an earlier engine" (EARLIER_WORDS, engine.py:140) and needs a replay again. It also needs a cardlog-check and new CHECKED/CHECKED_BUILDS/CHECKED_SOURCE (simjar.py:84-91).
- The claim "after that, fork AI fixes cost a paired experiment, not a replay" is therefore false unless the candidate also changes engine identity. Two ways to fix it:
  - (a) Key "forge" on the base release plus the game-changing patch ids in forge-patches.txt, not the commit. A commit whose new code is all default-off switches then adds no game-patch id. This needs a gate showing that seeded games play line for line the same as the previous build, like the 30+25-game identity check in HISTORY.md:664.
  - (b) Batch C4-C7 into one build, so there is one replay rather than one per fix.

What checks out:

The core diagnosis holds, but four claims are wrong and one of the three code changes needs rewriting.

**What holds (verified, in C:/VSProjects/forge/forge-ai/src/main/java/forge/ai/)**

- **ChangeZoneAi.java**
  - Lines 1141-1143: `doWithoutTarget` is true only when the ability is a planeswalker ability, uses targeting, has `getMinTargets()==0` and has a CostPutCounter cost.
  - Line 1145: `if (list.isEmpty() && !doWithoutTarget) return false;`.
  - Line 1231: the same flag is reused in the target loop, so redefining it at 1141 covers both places.
- **Both cards reach that check:**
  - Fiery Annihilation goes through `chkDrawback` (line 195), then `knownOriginPlayDrawbackAI` (839), then `isPreferredTarget(..., false, true)` (853).
  - Samwise the Stouthearted goes through checkETBEffects's `doTrigger(exSA, false)` (AiController:357), then `knownOriginTriggerAI` (1461), then `isPreferredTarget` (1494).
  - Both sub-abilities are `TargetMin$ 0` (f/fiery_annihilation.txt, s/samwise_the_stouthearted.txt).
  - The candidate says "Samwise" without a surname. The Samwise in TFP is Samwise the Stouthearted. Samwise Gamgee has no such sub.
- **DestroyAllAi.java:76-77:** `if (opplist.isEmpty()) return CantPlayAi`. It sits inside the per-opponent loop, before ailist is used at all.
  - Fires of Mount Doom's ChompEquip sub (`DestroyAll | ValidCards$ Targeted.Equipment+Attached`) is reached through `doTriggerNoCostWithSubs` and then `chkDrawbackWithSubs` (SpellAbilityAi.java:193-214, 269-281).
  - checkETBEffects is called for every permanent (AiController:992), not only creatures. So enchantments like Fires are vetoed too.
- **AiController.java:357-361:** the escape needs `api==null && card.isCreature() && !isFullyTargetable && (lifeInDanger || BadETB)`.
  - `ComputerUtilAbility.isFullyTargetable` (233-242) checks `getNumCandidates < getMinTargets`. That is 0 < 0, false, so it returns true for TargetMin 0, as claimed.
- **Fiery numbers match** overnight/2026-10-03/experiments/exp-m4-fiery/report.md: the arm without the override has 0.0% cast against the control's 90.1%, and the pooled matchup is -3.2 pts [-4.7, -1.6] over 800 games, not 1,600.
- **Fires control cast 0.0% matches** exp-overrides-etb/report.md:22.

**Corrections**

1. **The evidence numbers don't trace.**
   - "Fires 0.0% of 837": I can't find 837 in any report. r4-ai/notes.md:291 and v-r10/notes.md:64 say "0 of 685".
   - "Sunblast Angel 26.5%": also not found. r4-ai/notes.md:290 says 15% against Finneas and 49% against Calling All Angels. HISTORY.md:331 says 84% (Giada). The only 26.5% in the reports is an unrelated speed figure (REPORT.md:147).
   - Cite the real sources or drop these numbers.
2. **Plague Belcher and Victimize aren't covered.**
   - Plague Belcher's trigger is `PutCounter ... ValidTgts$ Creature.YouCtrl | IsCurse$ True` with the default TargetMin of 1 (p/plague_belcher.txt). It always has a candidate, itself, and it is decided in PutCounterAi, not in any of the three changed places.
   - Victimize is a sorcery (`SP$ Sacrifice`), not an enters-the-battlefield effect.
   - Massacre Wurm, which runs through PumpAllAi, isn't covered either. So the etb override set can't be retired completely.
3. **The AiController change at 359-361 contradicts itself and is too broad.**
   - "Skip the veto when ... it has no candidates" is exactly the Ravenous Chupacabra, Éowyn and Palace Jailer case: TargetMin 1 with no targets. The existing escape already handles that case behind lifeInDanger or BadETB. Skipping the veto there contradicts the stated carve-out.
   - "Skip when min targets is 0" would also hide every other reason `doTrigger` refused, such as a harmful mandatory sub or an unwanted cost later in the chain.
   - Once ChangeZoneAi is fixed, a TargetMin 0 trigger passes `doTrigger`, so this change is redundant. Drop it, or limit it to: every targeting step in the chain has `minTargets==0`, AND nothing else in the chain refused.
4. **Define the ChangeZoneAi condition as "the filtered list is empty", not "no candidates".**
   - Line 1145 tests the filtered `list`: opponents only for exile and bounce (1111-1123), then dying creatures removed and combat filters applied (1133-1138).
   - A `getNumCandidates()==0` test would still veto when candidates exist but all of them are filtered out.
   - Keep the change to AbilitySub only, as proposed. That leaves top-level "up to one target" spells and abilities vetoed, which is correct for them.
5. **The DestroyAllAi change must check both lists before line 76's early return**, which currently fires before ailist is looked at.
   - Sunblast Angel with only the AI's own creatures tapped stays vetoed, which is correct.
   - With no tapped creatures on either side it would now be cast in Main 1 as a 4/5 flyer. That is probably right, but expect its cast share to jump and judge it by "own lost per cast".
6. **Samwise has Flash.** The fix means it gets cast as a bare 2/1 plus Ring tempt whenever the AI feels like it, instead of being held for a turn when something of its own dies. "Cast more" isn't "plays better". Measure cast timing (the turn difference, and the share cast on an opponent's turn) as well as the cast share.
7. **There's no per-patch switch yet.** The fork's only switch is the global `-Ddecklab.gamePatches=off` (AiAttackController.java:68, Match.java:37), which also turns off deck-order-1 and the in-order attack checks. The `etb-harmless-1` switch needs a new per-id property plus an entry in forge-game's decklab/forge-patches.txt (d84031a6d's commit message). Count that in the effort.
8. **The measurement plan needs fixes.**
   - Run both arms with the `fiery` override, and the `etb` set's Fires and Samwise edits, turned off (the sets.json `fiery` set is adopted). Otherwise the script override hides the Java change.
   - The previous etb experiment needed about 2,800 games a pair to settle its two pairs (exp-overrides-etb/report.md: "more games"), so 1,600 may come back inconclusive.
   - TFP holds 1 Fires and 1 Samwise (deck_line: casual/the-free-peoples). That gives few drawn copies, so judge the cast share against the 685-copy baseline rather than expecting tight per-card ranges.
   - Gisa and Giada are `idea` Commander decks: Giada holds Sunblast Angel and Gisa holds Plague Belcher. Add Mono-White Angels or Orzhov Removal (Sunblast Angel in the sideboard) only with the sideboard in.
   - Include a no-change reference pair with none of these cards, to catch side effects on other enters effects.
9. **"Replaces the adopted Fiery override"** is right on rules accuracy. The override's `ChangeZoneAll ... Equipment.AttachedTo Targeted` exiles every attached Equipment (c1-completeness/notes.md:85), which the Java fix avoids. Retiring the override still needs an override-off run showing a cast share of about 90% or more.

Attack: aggression is set at AiAttackController.java:1239-1273 from ratioDiff. :1142-1145 decrements the AI's ratio once per opponent blocker, and attritional all-out needs ratioDiff > 0 (:1239). shouldAttack/SpellAbilityFactors (:1376-1565) judges each attacker against every blocker alone, with no blocker-count limit. Example: six 1/1s against two 2/2s gives aggression 2, so no 1/1 attacks.

TRICK_ATTACKERS memory (AiAttackController:1003-1011) forces remembered creatures to attack. AI card memory clears at the AI's own end step (PhaseHandler.java:363 calls PlayerControllerAi.resetAtEndOfTurn :1590-1593), so a per-turn mana reservation set clears itself.

Reserved mana is honoured in ComputerUtilMana.isManaSourceReserved (:1044-1085), called from canPayShardWithSpellAbility (:942), so reserved lands block both the decision and the payment. A new reservation check must come before the RESERVE_MANA_FOR_MAIN2_CHANCE roll at :1070.

Profile defaults (enum / Default.ai / Reckless.ai): PLAY_AGGRO false/false/true; CHANCE_TO_ATTACK_INTO_TRADE 40/0/100; CHANCE_TO_COUNTER_CMC_1 50/30/80; MIN_SPELL_CMC_TO_COUNTER 0/0/0 (2 in Cautious and Experimental); TRY_TO_HOLD_COMBAT_TRICKS_UNTIL_BLOCK false/true/true at 65%; RESERVE_MANA_FOR_MAIN2_CHANCE 0/100/100.
